steps.context: 12000 x 12 raw integer gene-level counts from salmon (first column gene symbol) and a 12-row metadata table (condition, batch). plan.title: Treated vs control DE in lung RNA-seq, confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative: The counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, salmon-derived integer counts) and metadata.csv (12 samples: condition, batch) describe 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples, but batch B1 holds every control and batch B2 holds every treated sample — the design matrix for condition + batch is not full rank, so batch cannot be modeled or removed (ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, SVA) without also removing the condition effect. The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) colored by both condition and batch to make the confounding visible rather than hidden; (2) runs the standard DESeq2 raw-count pipeline (minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, ~condition design with an explicit reference level, Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05), with edgeR QLF as a second method for a robustness overlap check, and every output explicitly labeled as confounded with batch — the 'treated vs control' signal is statistically indistinguishable from a 'B2 vs B1' processing effect; (3) runs over-representation analysis (not ranked GSEA, per the confounded-design rule) on the significant gene list against Hallmark/GO/Reactome gene sets using the tested genes as the universe, carrying the same confounding caveat forward. No step attempts to correct or hide the confound; the deliverable is a gene list with an explicit, unavoidable interpretive limitation.
